extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, naturalists, geographers, and public-health/education professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and implicit criteria for evaluating and reporting on scientific and popular scientific books, conference organization, and public-health/education practice as articulated in book reviews, letters, and reports. Focuses on accuracy, sources, illustrations, methods, and suitability for intended readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness and up-to-dateness of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The account's information should be trustworthy and up-to-date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer criticises a Tibet book for being 'neither very trustworthy nor up-to-date', noting that recent, more precise information should be used rather than antiquated sources. Up-to-date scientific research should be checked and used to correct older errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's personal knowledge and acquaintance with literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Author should have personal knowledge of the country/topic or be sufficiently acquainted with what has been written on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of personal experience or failure to read existing literature leads to frequent inaccuracies and lack of perspective; reviewers expect either firsthand experience or rigorous survey of the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of factual data (measurements, elevations, routes, maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual details such as elevations, relative altitudes, routes, and city elevations must be correct and based on trustworthy surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer gives concrete examples (Yamdok Lake elevation, Dumo Lake relative height, elevation of Lhasa) and criticises reliance on less accurate pioneer native surveyors when reliable British Survey officer measurements exist (Major Ryder). Map claims (e.g., 'best map we possess') should acknowledge superior, recent surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and relevance of included topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain focus on the principal theme; avoid dragging in heaps of irrelevant topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes that one-fifth of a Tibet book consists of extracts from unrelated missionary writings, and that the geographical theme is frequently lost sight of by inclusion of irrelevant material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and checking of sources versus later scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: Older or antiquated sources must be checked by comparison with later, more precise scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on antiquated sources without checking against newer findings propagates errors. The reviewer expects authors to correct or note earlier mistakes where later surveys provide better data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct naming, terminology, and orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive page headings and correct spellings (names, place-names) are expected; frequent misspelling is a fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer highlights frequent misspelling and wrongly rendered names (e.g., Chinese general 'Sand Fo' vs 'Sund Fô'), and incorrect labelling/choice of page headings as detracting from quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance, relevance, and originality of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should be original, closely connected with the letterpress, characteristic of the subject, and correctly attributed to the proper locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism where most illustrations had been seen elsewhere, were not closely connected with the text, landscapes not characteristic, and at least two images were from Sikkim, not Tibet. Reviewers expect illustrations to support the text and be correctly sourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological and factual accuracy in natural-history descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of biological fact (anatomy, life histories, species identity) must be accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of incorrect statements (eg echinoderms have a heart; Loligo media is the young of L. forbesii; incorrect mechanism for starfish opening casters) are cited as marbling an otherwise good book. Reviewers expect factual precision in natural-history treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generally accepted scientific nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should follow the nomenclature most generally in use in relevant groups (e.g., Pisces, Echinoderms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer disagrees that the author followed commonly used nomenclature, especially in certain taxa; incorrect or idiosyncratic naming is a fault and can mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical completeness and appropriateness of methodological/hardware advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of apparatus and field methods should be practical and complete for the intended activities and habitats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes omission of a crowbar in a shore-collector's outfit (surprising on a rocky coast) and criticises recommended tow-netting durations (half an hour too long if multiple collections placed in one bottle). Practical field advice should reflect common practice and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for intended audience and clear statement of limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be appropriate to their intended readership and state what they do or do not replace (e.g., they do not obviate need for monographs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite faults, reviewer recommends the shore-collecting book to beginners but stresses it does not replace access to detailed monographs on groups—authors/reviewers should clarify scope and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of photographic illustrations (technical execution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs should be in focus, well-composed, have appropriate backgrounds, and display good skill by the photographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer criticises many photographs as out of focus, of 'soot and sawdust' type, or with poor background choices that do not show the subject advantageously. Technical photographic quality affects usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical accuracy, especially scientific names
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical errors—particularly in scientific names—are serious faults and should be minimised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer enumerates errors (Nephtys for Nephthys; Maidae for Maiidae; Spangus for Spatangus) and regards such mistakes as maring professional credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of large-scale classification methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification methods (e.g., soil divisions) must be conceptually sound and appropriate for the scale of application; use of the same name for physically similar soils across continent should be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer questions the US soil survey's basis of physical texture and uniform naming across diverse origins, suggesting critics discredit both methods of identification/analysis and the rapidity with which work proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of survey resolution given resources/cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of detail and accuracy of a survey should be compatible with the resources expended (cost per square mile); too-low costs may yield only sketchy first approximations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes that when cost is less than 10s. per square mile, the resulting maps may be too sketchy; surveyors must match methodology and funding to desired accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of preliminary general accounts in applied surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary general accounts of physiography and agricultural development in survey reports are valuable to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if maps are sketchy, English readers benefit from general accounts that sketch farming style and local conditions—reports should include accessible, contextual summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with prevailing authoritative views in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should acknowledge and, where appropriate, align or contrast their views with those held by most authorities in the subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer points out that Dr. Lapponi's views on hypnosis differ from most authorities; divergence is acceptable but should be clearly argued and justified to be persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about personal experience and evidence basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be clear about whether claims are based on personal experience, testimony of others, or secondary reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Lapponi 'honestly states that he has not had personal experience' of spirit phenomena but is convinced of their existence; reviewers note such distinctions and weigh evidentiary bases accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of fraud, illusions, and alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of extraordinary phenomena should consider and rigorously address possible explanations such as fraud, illusion, and unconscious deception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author concedes some spiritistic cases are explained by illusions or frauds (voluntary or unconscious) but still considers some phenomena 'well authenticated'—reviewers expect stronger arguments to exclude mundane explanations before accepting extraordinary claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and practical evaluation of phenomena (danger, harm)
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors render ethical or practical judgments (e.g., spiritism is dangerous/immoral), such claims should be supported by reasoned argument, not merely assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer finds the author's final denunciation of spiritism ('always dangerous, harmful, immoral... to be condemned') too sweeping; strong moral conclusions should be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological awareness in observational physics (account for motion when interpreting timings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When deducing physical constants from astronomical timings (e.g., velocity of light from occultations), one must account for motions of observer and source (earth, Jupiter) relative to the medium (aether) to first order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter notes that observed times of occultation are affected by Earth's and Jupiter's motion relative to the aether and that analysis should search for systematic direction-dependent differences; small corrections for planetary motion along lines of centres and conditioning of components should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical inspection as keystone of school physical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical inspection in schools is essential for physical education because it identifies defects (eyes, ears, nose, teeth) that impair learning and later fitness for occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sir Lauder Brunton calls medical inspection 'the keystone of physical education'—without it defects remain undetected, harming learning and long-term prospects; school-health programs should prioritise regular medical checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining mental education with physical training; alternation and nature of exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational work must be combined with appropriate physical training using proper alternation of mental and physical exercise and attention to the nature of physical activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither games-only nor exercise-only approaches are ideal; an appropriate combination and proper alternation prevent injury and maximise overall development. Systematic exercise develops muscles; games develop different faculties—balance both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction in laws of health by demonstration rather than lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching children hygiene and health laws should be by actual demonstration rather than by lecture, which may be misunderstood or forgotten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sir Lauder Brunton recommends demonstrative instruction to teach cleanliness, dangers of impure food/water, and evils of alcohol; pedagogical methods matter for retention and behaviour change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term / generational perspective in child-health policy
rubrics_metrics.description: School and child-health policies should consider long-term generational effects; the health and upbringing of current children determine the physique of future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President notes it's vital to look fifteen or twenty years ahead since current schoolchildren will become parents; preventive measures and early instruction have cascading effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for successful scientific meetings and association arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful scientific meeting requires a good venue choice, high character of proceedings, careful arrangements for convenience and comfort, clear directions and maps, and social elements subordinate to scientific work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report praises Leicester meeting for these qualities: thoughtful local arrangements, informative programme materials, good sectional papers, well-managed social events that do not overshadow the advancement of science.
